text:
Interview notes, a thirty-minute call with an engineering manager of eight years, taken by the
author during the call.

label: aside
text:
Considered: the manager reviewed these notes afterwards and corrected two
lines.

label: claim
source: interview with an engineering manager of eight years
text: - Her rule: the report owns the agenda.

label: claim
source: interview with an engineering manager of eight years
text:
She keeps a shared document per person; they add items
  before the meeting, and she adds hers last, at the bottom.

label: quote
speaker: the engineering manager interviewed
text: - "If I have something urgent, it is not a one-on-one topic. I send it the day it happens."

label: claim
source: interview with an engineering manager of eight years
text:
- The first one-on-one with a new report is always the same: she asks how they like to receive
  feedback, in writing or out loud, right away or at the end of the week.

label: claim
source: interview with an engineering manager of eight years
text: - Her warning: new managers treat silence as a problem.

label: quote
speaker: the engineering manager interviewed
text:
"Wait. Count to five. The real answer is
  the second one."

label: claim
source: interview with an engineering manager of eight years
text: - She cancels a one-on-one only when the report asks her to, never on her own.
